24456-fathers-of-biology.description: A book by CHARLES McRAE, M.A., F.L.S.. He was probably born about 470 B.C., and, according to all accounts, appears to have reached the advanced age of ninety years or more. He must, therefore, have lived during a period of Greek history which was characterized by great intellectual activity; for he had, as his contemporaries, Pericles the famous statesman; the poets Æschylus, Sophocles, Euripides, Aristophanes, and Pindar; the philosopher Socrates, with his disciples Xenophon and Plato; the historians Herodotus and Thucydides; and Phidias the unrivalled sculptor.

arxiv-1702-06029.title: Bayesian regression of piecewise homogeneous Poisson processes Volume: 7
arxiv-1702-06029.creator: Diego J. R. Sevilla [ inst1 ]
arxiv-1702-06029.description: Abstract \articlenumber 070018 \journalyear 2015 \editor R. Dickman \reviewers M. Hutter, Australian National University, Canberra, Australia. 070018 \pipabstract In this paper, a Bayesian method for piecewise regression is adapted to handle counting processes data distributed as Poisson. A numerical code in Mathematica is developed and tested analyzing simulated data.

arxiv-1907-01669.title: MultiWOZ 2.1: A Consolidated Multi-Domain Dialogue Dataset with State Corrections and State Tracking Baselines
arxiv-1907-01669.description: Abstract MultiWOZ 2.0 [ \citenameBudzianowski et al.2018 ] is a recently released multi-domain dialogue dataset spanning 7 distinct domains and containing over 10,000 dialogues. Though immensely useful and one of the largest resources of its kind to-date, MultiWOZ 2.0 has a few shortcomings.

arxiv-2101-11418.title: Spectrum Sharing for 6G Integrated Satellite-Terrestrial Communication Networks Based on NOMA and Cognitive Radio
arxiv-2101-11418.creator: Xin Liu, Kwok-Yan Lam, Feng Li, Jun Zhao, Li Wang
arxiv-2101-11418.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Xin Liu, Kwok-Yan Lam, Feng Li, Jun Zhao, Li Wang. The explosive growth of bandwidth hungry Internet applications has led to the rapid development of new generation mobile network technologies that are expected to provide broadband access to the Internet in a pervasive manner. For example, 6G networks are capable of providing high-speed network access by exploiting higher frequency spectrum; high-throughout satellite communication services are also adopted to achieve pervasive coverage in remote and isolated areas.

arxiv-2110-04421.title: DeepABM: SCALABLE, EFFICIENT AND DIFFERENTIABLE AGENT-BASED SIMULATIONS VIA GRAPH NEURAL NETWORKS
arxiv-2110-04421.creator: Ayush Chopra Ramesh Raskar Media Lab Massachusetts Institute of Technology 75 Amherst St Cambridge, MA 02139, USA, Esma S. Gel School of Comp, Inf. and Decision Systems Eng. Arizona State University 699 S Mill Avenue Tempe, AZ 85281, USA, Jayakumar Subramanian Balaji Krishnamurthy Media and Data Sci
arxiv-2110-04421.description: Abstract \WSCpagesetup Chopra, Gel, Subramanian, Krishnamurthy, Romero-Brufau, Pasupathy, Kingsley, and Raskar ABSTRACT We introduce DeepABM, a framework for agent-based modeling that leverages geometric message passing of graph neural networks for simulating action and interactions over large agent populations. Using DeepABM allows scaling simulations to large agent populations in real-time and running them efficiently on GPU architectures.

arxiv-2308-07285.title: Electronic states in a quantum Beltrami surface
arxiv-2308-07285.creator: J. Furtado
arxiv-2308-07285.description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate the influence of the geometry in the electronic states of a quantum Beltrami surface. We have considered an electron governed by the spinless stationary Schrödinger equation constrained to move on the Beltrami surface due to a confining potential from which the Da Costa potential emerges.

arxiv-2407-15857.title: BoRA: Bayesian Hierarchical Low-Rank Adaptation for Multi-Task Large Language Models
arxiv-2407-15857.creator: Simen Eide, Arnoldo Frigessi
arxiv-2407-15857.description: Abstract This paper introduces Bayesian Hierarchical Low-Rank Adaptation (BoRA), a novel method for fine-tuning multi-task Large Language Models (LLMs). Current fine-tuning approaches, such as Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), perform exceptionally well in reducing training parameters and memory usage but face limitations when applied to multiple similar tasks.

arxiv-2505-21985.title: Reward-Independent Messaging for Decentralized Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2505-21985.creator: Naoto Yoshida, Tadahiro Taniguchi
arxiv-2505-21985.description: Abstract In multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), effective communication improves agent performance, particularly under partial observability. We propose MARL-CPC, a framework that enables communication among fully decentralized, independent agents without parameter sharing. MARL-CPC incorporates a message learning model based on collective predictive coding (CPC) from emergent communication research.

arxiv-2512-15502.title: Lower Bounding the Secret Key Capacity of Bosonic Gaussian Channels via Optimal Gaussian Measurements
arxiv-2512-15502.creator: Giuseppe Ortolano 1,2, Stefano Pirandola 3, Leonardo Banchi 1,2
arxiv-2512-15502.description: Abstract We find the maximum rate achievable in the private communication over a bosonic quantum channel with a fully Gaussian protocol based on optimal single-mode Gaussian measurements. This rate establishes a lower bound on the secret rate capacity of the channel. We focus on the class of phase-insensitive Gaussian channels.

pmc-10670664.title: Work Fluctuations in Ergotropic Heat Engines
pmc-10670664.creator: Giovanni Chesi, Chiara Macchiavello, Massimiliano Federico Sacchi
pmc-10670664.description: We study the work fluctuations in ergotropic heat engines, namely two-stroke quantum Otto engines where the work stroke is designed to extract the ergotropy (the maximum amount of work by a cyclic unitary evolution) from a couple of quantum systems at canonical equilibrium at two different temperatures, whereas the heat stroke thermalizes back the systems to their respective reservoirs.

pmc-10674729.title: Randomized Controlled Trials to Treat Obesity in Military Populations: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-10674729.creator: Davide Gravina, Johanna Louise Keeler, Melahat Nur Akkese, Sevgi Bektas, Paula Fina, Charles Tweed, Gerd-Dieter Willmund, Janet Treasure, Hubertus Himmerich, Arved Weimann
pmc-10674729.description: In recent years, overweight and obesity have reached an alarmingly high incidence and prevalence worldwide; they have also been steadily increasing in military populations. Military personnel, as an occupational group, are often exposed to stressful and harmful environments that represent a risk factor for disordered eating, with major repercussions on both physical and mental health.

pmc-11321093.title: Major dietary patterns and their associations with total weight loss and weight loss composition 2–4 years after sleeve gastrectomy
pmc-11321093.creator: Nazanin Moslehi, Zahra Kamali, Maryam Barzin, Alireza Khalaj, Parvin Mirmiran
pmc-11321093.description: BackgroundFood intakes 1–2 years following bariatric surgery depend more on patients than the surgery’s gastrointestinal tract changes. This study aimed to determine the major dietary patterns of patients after the first two years of sleeve gastrectomy and to investigate their associations with total weight loss (TWL) and the proportion of TWL as fat mass (FM) and fat-free mass (FFM) loss.

pmc-11396051.title: Rheumatic heart disease on an Eastern Arizona Reservation, 2007-2022
pmc-11396051.creator: Jacob Hoekzema, LeCario Benashley, Ryan Close, Andrea Beaton, Sarah de Loizaga
pmc-11396051.description: Contemporary studies of rheumatic heart disease (RHD) within American Indian communities are lacking, despite recent work indicating high rates of group A streptococcus, the precursor to RHD. Utilizing retrospective chart review of the Indian Health Service, we sought to characterize the burden of acute rheumatic fever and RHD within an American Indian tribe in Eastern Arizona.

pmc-11546416.title: Characterization of Cytoskeletal Profilin Genes in Plasticity Elongation of Mesocotyl and Coleoptile of Maize Under Diverse Abiotic Stresses
pmc-11546416.creator: Xiaoqiang Zhao, Siqi Sun, Zhenzhen Shi, Fuqiang He, Guoxiang Qi, Xin Li, Yining Niu, Hunseung Kang, Dong-Gwan Kim
pmc-11546416.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The plasticity elongation of mesocotyl (MES) and coleoptile (COL) largely determines the morphology of maize seedlings under abiotic stresses. The profilin (PRF) proteins play a pivotal role in cytoskeleton dynamics and plant development via regulating actin polymerization. However, little is known about whether and how the expression of the ZmPRF gene family regulates MES and COL elongation in maize under adverse abiotic stresses. Here, a total of eight ZmPRF gene members were identified in the maize genome.

pmc-11677800.title: Targeting Iron Responsive Elements (IREs) of APP mRNA into Novel Therapeutics to Control the Translation of Amyloid-β Precursor Protein in Alzheimer’s Disease
pmc-11677800.creator: Mateen A. Khan
pmc-11677800.description: The hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the buildup of amyloid-β (Aβ), which is produced when the amyloid precursor protein (APP) misfolds and deposits as neurotoxic plaques in the brain. A functional iron responsive element (IRE) RNA stem loop is encoded by the APP 5′-UTR and may be a target for regulating the production of Alzheimer’s amyloid precursor protein.

pmc-12598672.title: Cost-Effectiveness of One-time Universal Testing for Hepatitis D Among Adults With Chronic Hepatitis B in the United States
pmc-12598672.creator: Mehlika Toy, David Hutton, Eyasu Teshale, William W Thompson, Hang Pham, Joshua A Salomon, Samuel So
pmc-12598672.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundChronic hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection increases the risk of liver-related deaths in adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). In the United States (US), only an estimated 12.9% of adults with CHB have received an HDV antibody test.

pmc-12636004.title: Visualizing the Invisible: Dual Click Imaging of Ruthenium-Based Photoactivated Chemotherapy Agents and Their DNA Synthesis Inhibition in Fixed Cancer Cells
pmc-12636004.creator: Anja Busemann, Lisa Rieger, Rachael M. Cunningham, Sam C. Davidse, Irene Regeni, Ingrid Flaspohler, Claudia Schmidt, Xue-Quan Zhou, Vincent van Rixel, Maxime A. Siegler, Ingo Ott, Sylvia E. Le Dévédec, Hans-Achim Wagenknecht, Victoria J. DeRose, Sylvestre Bonnet
pmc-12636004.description: Like many drugs, ruthenium-based photoactivated chemotherapy (PACT) complexes are hard to follow in cells due to their absence of emissive properties. Here, two alkyne-functionalized Ru-based PACT compounds with the formula [Ru­(HCC-tpy)­(N̂N)­(Hmte)]­(PF6)2 were synthesized, where HCC-tpy = 4′-ethynyl-2,2′:6′,2″-terpyridine, N̂N = 3,3′-biisoquinoline (i-biq, [2]­(PF6)2) or di­(isoquinolin-3-yl)­amine (i-Hdiqa, [4]­(PF6)2), and Hmte = 2-(methylthio)­ethanol.

pmc-12828016.title: Whole-genome sequencing GWAS reveals bovine genomic effects on enteric methane emissions in beef cattle
pmc-12828016.creator: Leonardo M Arikawa, Lucio F M Mota, Larissa F S Fonseca, Gerardo A Fernandes Júnior, Sindy L C Nasner, Júlia P S Valente, Tainara L S Soares, Marcelo S Borges, Joel A Silva, Amalia M Pelaez, Maria E Z Mercadante, Lucia G Albuquerque
pmc-12828016.description: The world has recognized the significance of sustainable animal production, especially in terms of mitigating methane emissions. Developing strategies to mitigate methane without compromising productivity presents a significant challenge for nutritionists and breeders. However, measuring methane emissions at the individual level can be expensive and laborious.

pmc-13072032.title: In Vitro Evaluation of Spearmint Essential Oil (Mentha spicata L.) Supplementation on Gas Production, Rumen Fermentation, and Microbial Community Structure
pmc-13072032.creator: Chengzhen Huang, Jiamin Chen, Lin Wang, Lei Wang, Jiayi Li, Lifeng Dong
pmc-13072032.description: Simple SummaryExtensive enteric methane mitigation approaches have been developed to alleviate anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions and increase energy utilization efficiency in ruminant production. In this study, we investigated whether spearmint essential oil (SEO) could reduce methane production during rumen fermentation. Using an in vitro rumen fermentation system, different doses of SEO were evaluated.

pmc-13287852.title: 5Targeting Pin1 in cholangiocarcinoma tumor and stromal cells using siRNA therapeutics
pmc-13287852.creator: Justin H Lo, Thatcher R Heumann, Nora Francini, Eva F Gbur, Michelle Zhou, Shabnam Z Eghbali, Laura W Goff, Craig L Duvall
pmc-13287852.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and ObjectivesPin1 (peptidyl-prolyl isomerase, NIMA-interacting 1) overexpression in tumor cells and stroma has been associated with poor clinical outcomes and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment in pancreatic cancer. Hypothesizing that Pin1 could have a similar role in cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), we sought to investigate the therapeutic potential of silencing Pin1 using small interfering RNA (siRNA), leveraging a tumor-tropic siRNA-lipid conjugate design termed siRNA-L2.MethodssiRNA/siRNA-L2 sequences were synthesized on a MerMade oligonucleotide synthesizer and dosed in vitro at 100 nM (with lipofectamine) or 1 μM

pmc-13655914.title: Video-assisted thoracoscopic diaphragmatic plication in a ventilator-dependent patient with an elevated and dysfunctional hemidiaphragm
pmc-13655914.creator: Fangyuan Li, Chengqiang Li, Hecheng Li
pmc-13655914.description: Unilateral hemidiaphragm dysfunction can reduce ventilatory reserve, but its contribution to weaning failure is difficult to isolate in a critically ill patient. A 61-year-old woman with asthma and a chronically elevated left hemidiaphragm developed severe pneumonia and acute hypercapnic respiratory failure, with an arterial partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PaCO2) of 164.

pmc-13673367.title: Integration of molecular and cellular immunity in sea cucumbers: a comprehensive review
pmc-13673367.creator: Noé Wambreuse, Guillaume Caulier, Jérôme Delroisse, Igor Eeckhaut
pmc-13673367.description: Highlights•Molecular and cellular levels of sea cucumber immunity are currently studied separately.•108 immune genes are reported, including 74 functionally characterised.•10 main coelomocyte morphotypes are reported and classified between confirmed (5), controversial (3) and uncertain cell morphotypes (2).•Most studies on the immunology of sea cucumbers focus on Apostichopus japonicus, reflecting the need for a higher diversity of model species.
